title: Official 2026 NFC East Prediction: 1. Eagles: There are four parts of the team I feel really good about with the Eagles entering 2026 — Nick Sirianni, Jalen Hurts, the defense and the running game. I think those four are enough to win the division. The offense overall is a question but I feel better about the Eagles offense than I do the Cowboys defense. 2. Cowboys: The best unit in the entire NFC might be the Cowboys offense. That alone should make the NFC East race interesting. The two things holding me back from picking the Cowboys to win the division are their defense and how reliant they are on Dak Prescott. If Prescott goes down their season is cooked. The defense at best could be like 20th in the NFL. That won’t be enough to overtake the Eagles. 3. Giants: I’m in on the Giants this year. Harbaugh should make them a competent team again. The close losses last year should turn to close wins. I also think Jaxson Dart is good and with Malik Nabers back their offense should be legit. The backend of the defense though (plus Dart’s reckless play could cause him to miss some games) keeps them from the playoffs. 4. Commanders: This season has disaster written all over it for the Commanders. Their defense is terrible, their offensive line is a mess and they have two new first-team coordinators. Jayden Daniels is the only wild card that keeps me from picking them as one of the worst teams in the entire league.

title: The New Orleans Saints organization is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of WWL Radio host Mike Detillier. A proud son of Louisiana, Mike was widely respected as a gifted football analyst, a trusted guide through the NFL Draft, and an exceptional family man. Beyond his incredible contributions to the game, he was above all a true gentleman and a dedicated family man. Saints gamedays at the Caesars Superdome, training camp practices, and press conferences simply will not be the same without his presence. Our thoughts and prayers go out to his immediate family and to the community of devoted listeners who considered him a friend over the airwaves.

"Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success. As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success. Robert Kraft (Chairman) John Mara Shad Khan Jimmy Haslam Michael Bidwill Greg Penner

As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. 
 
Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success.  To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. 
 
We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years.
 
If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us.

title: The below memorandum that was sent to the full membership this afternoon by Robert Kraft, chairman of the Compensation Committee: “September 6, 2026 “As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. “Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success. To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. “We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years. If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us. Robert Kraft (Chairman) John Mara Shad Khan Jimmy Haslam Michael Bidwill Greg Penner”.
summary:
The below memorandum that was sent to the full membership this afternoon by Robert Kraft, chairman of the Compensation Committee:
 
“September 6, 2026
 
“As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. 
 
“Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success.  To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. 
 
“We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years.
 
If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us.
 
Robert Kraft (Chairman)
John Mara
Shad Khan
Jimmy Haslam
Michael Bidwill
Greg Penner”.
full_text:
The below memorandum that was sent to the full membership this afternoon by Robert Kraft, chairman of the Compensation Committee:
 
“September 6, 2026
 
“As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. 
 
“Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success.  To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. 
 
“We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years.
 
If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us.
 
Robert Kraft (Chairman)
